In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the carrier ligands studied are not only capable of forming complexes with metal cations but also bind strongly to protein sites of HSA.
the carrier ligands are bound to the protein at sites I and/or II, depending on the ligand, with a preference for the former site.
all the ligands bind to both binding sites, but with different affinities, and the binding to site II is the most dominant.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
dipic and 2,6-dimethylpyridine-3,5-dicarboxylic (dipicm) bind strongly at site I of HSA and pic and 6-Me pic bind at site I and II.
the binding of the ligands at the two sites of HSA is not only dependent on the nature of the metal ion but also on the nature of ligand.
the carrier ligands bind to HSA with high affinity, which is important to consider when designing antidiabetic metal drugs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the carrier ligands bind in a competitive fashion with site I markers, and in a non-competitive manner with site II markers, and the binding is influenced by the presence of the metal ion.
the carrier ligands bind to HSA and thus, the complexes may interact with the drug binding pockets of HSA.
the binding of carrier ligand to HSA may influence the bioavailability of the metal ion and hence the therapeutic efficacy.
